narrative: Material PL2__ME04FCDD exhibits lumpy demand (CV=0.55) with a mild declining trend of -1.36 units/day and unstable lead times (CV=1.40) driven by a single 2.43-day outlier. The safety stock is raised from SAP's 160 to 201 units to correctly cover combined lead-time-demand variability at 95% service level. The economic order quantity of 8,335 units is hard-capped to 2,146 units by the 2,347-unit storage constraint, forcing ~30 orders/year vs. the optimal ~8, which increases total annual cost by $1,246. Expanding storage capacity is the primary lever to unlock true EOQ economics.
warnings: Order quantity constrained by storage capacity from 8335 to 2146 units
Lead time CV=1.40 indicates unstable supplier performance; one outlier of 2.43 days strongly influences variability

research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy but mostly non-zero demand (94.8%) with very short mean lead time (0.27 days) suits a continuous-review (r,Q) policy where inventory is monitored continuously and a fixed quantity Q is ordered whenever stock hits the reorder point r. The EOQ minimises total replenishment and holding cost; capacity capping is applied as a hard constraint.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is fully saturated (100%). The capacity cap reduces order quantity from 8,335 to 2,146, increasing annual ordering cost by $1,671 while saving only $424 in holding cost, netting a $1,246 cost penalty. Service level integrity is maintained but any upward demand spike could cause stockouts given the constrained replenishment cycle.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Storage expansion review recommended. Current max_storage_units=2347 prevents economic ordering. MOQ (166) + safety_stock (201) = 367 < 2347, so no MOQ-capacity infeasibility exists, but true EOQ is infeasible at current capacity.
